newsitem.title: USA: Quality Dining not for sale - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Quality Dining not for sale - CEO.

text.p: Quality Dining Inc Chief Executive Daniel Fitzpatrick on Friday said the company was not for sale.
But also Friday, the company reappointed two former board members who had resigned after expressing displeasure with the company's plans for its Bruegger's Bagel Bakery unit.
"Quality Dining is not for sale and there will not be an auction of the company," Fitzpatrick said in a statement.
Quality Dining also said eight of the 11 board members thought a sale of the company was not in its best interest.

The dissenters included Nordahl Brue and Michael Dressell, founders of Bruegger's, who resigned from the board last month. The third was David Austin, a Brue and Dressell nominee who was placed on the board Friday.

The statement from Fitzpatrick and the company was in response to a Securities and Exchange Commission filing made by Brue and Dressell earlier this week. In the filing, they said they had hired an investment firm to consider options for Quality Dining, which last year bought Bruegger's.
The management of "the company does not have a viable plan to grow, or to finance the growth of, its business as owner, operator and franchisor of Bruegger's Bagel Bakery...," the SEC filing said.
Quality Dining Treasurer David Findlay said Brue and Dressell were reappointed to the board on Friday at their request.

In the statement regarding the company not being for sale, Quality Dining said it invited Brue, Dressell and Austin to join the company's board to participate in constructively managing the company's affairs. "The company expects that they will do so," the statment said.
Quality Dining shares rose 5/8 to 13-1/8 Friday.
